name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MATCH_Q01 - Hormones and their source endocrine glands

questiontext.text:
Match the hormones listed in the left column with their respective source endocrine glands in the right column:

HormoneSource Gland
A. \(\mathrm{T}_4\) (Thyroxine)(i) Hypothalamus
B. PTH (Parathyroid hormone)(ii) Thyroid
C. GnRH (Gonadotrophin releasing hormone)(iii) Pituitary
D. LH (Luteinizing hormone)(iv) Parathyroid

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each organised endocrine gland in the human body synthesises and secretes specific hormones that regulate target tissues.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
Thyroxine (\(\mathrm{T}_4\)) is synthesised by the follicular cells of the thyroid gland. Parathyroid hormone (PTH) is a peptide hormone secreted by the parathyroid glands. Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) is produced by neurosecretory cells of the hypothalamus to stimulate the pituitary. Luteinizing hormone (LH) is a gonadotrophin produced by the pars distalis (anterior pituitary).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: \(\mathrm{T}_4\) with Thyroid, PTH with Parathyroid, GnRH with Hypothalamus, and LH with Pituitary (A-ii, B-iv, C-i, D-iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MATCH_Q02 - Pituitary hormones and their physiological functions

questiontext.text:
Match each pituitary hormone with its primary physiological function:

Pituitary HormonePhysiological Function
A. Prolactin (PRL)(i) Acts on melanocytes to regulate skin pigmentation
B. Melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH)(ii) Resorption of water and electrolytes by distal renal tubules
C. Oxytocin(iii) Growth of mammary glands and formation of milk
D. Vasopressin (ADH)(iv) Vigorous contraction of uterus at childbirth and milk ejection

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The pituitary gland secretes hormones from the adenohypophysis (pars distalis and pars intermedia) and releases neurohypophyseal hormones stored in the pars nervosa.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
Prolactin (PRL) from the anterior pituitary regulates the growth of mammary glands and formation of milk in them. Melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH) from the pars intermedia acts on melanocytes (melanin-containing cells) to regulate skin pigmentation. Oxytocin from the posterior pituitary acts on smooth muscles to stimulate vigorous uterine contractions during childbirth and milk ejection from the mammary gland. Vasopressin (ADH) acts mainly at the kidney to stimulate resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-iii, B-i, C-iv, D-ii.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MATCH_Q03 - Endocrine disorders and their hormonal causes

questiontext.text:
Match the following endocrine disorders with their corresponding hormonal causes:

DisorderHormonal Cause
A. Acromegaly(i) Hyperthyroidism with protrusion of eyeballs
B. Diabetes Insipidus(ii) Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults
C. Graves' disease(iii) Underproduction of hormones by adrenal cortex
D. Addison's disease(iv) Impairment in synthesis or release of ADH

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hyposecretion or hypersecretion of hormones from endocrine glands leads to characteristic physiological disorders.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
Acromegaly results from excess secretion of growth hormone in adults, especially in middle age, causing severe disfigurement of the face. Diabetes Insipidus is caused by an impairment affecting the synthesis or release of anti-diuretic hormone (ADH), reducing the kidney's ability to conserve water. Graves' disease (exophthalmic goitre) is a form of hyperthyroidism characterised by thyroid enlargement, protrusion of eyeballs, increased basal metabolic rate, and weight loss. Addison's disease results from underproduction of hormones by the adrenal cortex, altering carbohydrate metabolism and causing acute weakness and fatigue.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-ii, B-iv, C-i, D-iii.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MATCH_Q04 - Adrenal cortex layers and corticoid functions

questiontext.text:
Match the adrenal cortex layers and hormones with their correct descriptions:

Structure / HormoneDescription
A. Zona glomerulosa(i) Middle layer of adrenal cortex
B. Zona fasciculata(ii) Main glucocorticoid producing anti-inflammatory reactions
C. Aldosterone(iii) Outer layer of adrenal cortex
D. Cortisol(iv) Stimulates \(\mathrm{Na}^+\) reabsorption and \(\mathrm{K}^+\) excretion

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The adrenal cortex is organised into three concentric layers and secretes corticoid hormones, mainly glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
From outside to inside, the three layers of the adrenal cortex are zona glomerulosa (outer layer), zona fasciculata (middle layer), and zona reticularis (inner layer). Aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid in the human body; it acts at the renal tubules to stimulate reabsorption of \(\mathrm{Na}^+\) and water and excretion of \(\mathrm{K}^+\) and phosphate ions. Cortisol is the main glucocorticoid, which stimulates gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, and proteolysis, produces anti-inflammatory reactions, and suppresses the immune response.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-iii, B-i, C-iv, D-ii.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MATCH_Q05 - Endocrine cells of pancreas and gonads with secreted hormones

questiontext.text:
Match the following endocrine cells or structures with the hormones they secrete:

Cell / StructureSecreted Hormone
A. \(\alpha\)-cells of Islets of Langerhans(i) Androgens (mainly testosterone)
B. \(\beta\)-cells of Islets of Langerhans(ii) Glucagon
C. Leydig cells of testis(iii) Progesterone
D. Corpus luteum of ovary(iv) Insulin

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Specific hormone-producing cells within the endocrine pancreas and gonads secrete peptide or steroid hormones.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
In the Islets of Langerhans of the pancreas, \(\alpha\)-cells secrete the hyperglycemic hormone glucagon, whereas \(\beta\)-cells secrete the hypoglycemic hormone insulin. In the testis, Leydig (interstitial) cells located in the intertubular spaces produce androgens, mainly testosterone. In the ovary, the ruptured follicle after ovulation transforms into the corpus luteum, which secretes mainly progesterone.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-ii, B-iv, C-i, D-iii.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MATCH_Q06 - Hormones of heart, kidney, and gastrointestinal tract

questiontext.text:
Match the peptide hormones secreted by non-endocrine tissues with their physiological actions:

HormonePhysiological Action
A. Atrial natriuretic factor (ANF)(i) Stimulates secretion of HCl and pepsinogen
B. Erythropoietin(ii) Stimulates formation of red blood cells
C. Gastrin(iii) Stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions from pancreas
D. Secretin(iv) Dilates blood vessels to decrease blood pressure

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Certain non-endocrine organs such as the heart, kidney, and gastrointestinal tract also secrete peptide hormones that regulate cardiovascular, haematopoietic, and digestive processes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
Atrial natriuretic factor (ANF), secreted by the atrial wall of the heart when blood pressure rises, causes dilation of blood vessels and lowers blood pressure. Erythropoietin, produced by the juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney, stimulates erythropoiesis (RBC formation). Gastrin acts on gastric glands to stimulate the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen. Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas to stimulate secretion of water and bicarbonate ions.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-iv, B-ii, C-i, D-iii.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MATCH_Q07 - Gastrointestinal hormones, growth factors, and thymosins

questiontext.text:
Match each regulatory factor or hormone with its specific biological effect:

Hormone / FactorBiological Effect
A. Cholecystokinin (CCK)(i) Inhibits gastric secretion and motility
B. Gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP)(ii) Promotes T-lymphocyte differentiation and antibody production
C. Growth factors(iii) Stimulates secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice
D. Thymosins(iv) Essential for normal growth, repair, and regeneration of tissues

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Gastrointestinal peptide hormones, tissue growth factors, and thymic peptide hormones carry out specialised regulatory roles.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
Cholecystokinin (CCK) acts on both the pancreas and gall bladder to stimulate the secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice, respectively. Gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP) inhibits gastric secretion and motility. Growth factors secreted by non-endocrine tissues are essential for the normal growth of tissues and their repairing or regeneration. Thymosins from the thymus gland play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes (cell-mediated immunity) and also promote antibody production (humoral immunity).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-iii, B-i, C-iv, D-ii.

questiontext.text:
Match the chemical classes of hormones with their representative examples:

Chemical ClassRepresentative Examples
A. Peptide / protein hormones(i) Thyroxine (\(\mathrm{T}_4\))
B. Steroids(ii) Insulin and glucagon
C. Iodothyronines(iii) Epinephrine
D. Amino-acid derivatives(iv) Cortisol and estradiol

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
On the basis of their chemical nature, hormones are divided into four groups: peptide/polypeptide/protein hormones, steroids, iodothyronines, and amino-acid derivatives.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
Insulin, glucagon, pituitary hormones, and hypothalamic hormones are peptide, polypeptide, or protein hormones. Cortisol, testosterone, estradiol, and progesterone are steroid hormones. Thyroid hormones such as thyroxine (\(\mathrm{T}_4\)) are iodothyronines. Epinephrine (adrenaline) is an amino-acid derivative.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-ii, B-iv, C-i, D-iii.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MATCH_Q09 - Regulatory roles of pineal, thyroid, and parathyroid hormones

questiontext.text:
Match the following hormones with their characteristic regulatory roles:

HormoneRegulatory Role
A. Melatonin(i) Protein hormone that lowers blood calcium levels
B. Thyrocalcitonin (TCT)(ii) Regulates basal metabolic rate and supports RBC formation
C. Parathyroid hormone (PTH)(iii) Regulates 24-hour diurnal rhythm and sleep-wake cycle
D. Thyroxine (\(\mathrm{T}_4\))(iv) Peptide hormone that stimulates bone resorption to raise blood \(\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hormones from the pineal, thyroid, and parathyroid glands maintain diurnal rhythms, metabolic rate, and calcium homeostasis.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
Melatonin secreted by the pineal gland plays a key role in regulating the 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of the body, including the sleep-wake cycle and body temperature. Thyrocalcitonin (TCT) is a protein hormone secreted by the thyroid gland that decreases blood calcium levels. Parathyroid hormone (PTH) is a peptide hormone that stimulates bone resorption, renal \(\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}\) reabsorption, and intestinal \(\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}\) absorption to increase blood \(\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}\) levels. Thyroxine (\(\mathrm{T}_4\)) regulates the basal metabolic rate, supports erythropoiesis (RBC formation), and controls carbohydrate, protein, and fat metabolism.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-iii, B-i, C-iv, D-ii.
